summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated remote-controlled daemon with PTY/shell channel
details: The package's `main` and `bin whalent-core` entry point `dist/index.cjs` is a ~13 MB bundle wrapped in obfuscator.io string-array + rotator + decoder obfuscation (`_0x0xXXXX` identifiers, 106585-entry string array, numeric-expression index math). No plaintext URLs, hostnames, or protocol strings remain in the bundle; only the token `whalent` and a fragment `upgrade.` are visible. The bundle imports `ws`/`WebSocket`, `child_process`, `spawn(`, `ssh2`, and optional `node-pty` — the composition of a network-driven shell/PTY control channel on the installer's host. The package's own README describes the runtime as being 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades', i.e., an author-controlled remote code-push channel outside the npm publish path that loads and executes new code on installed hosts. Obfuscation of every network destination combined with an inbound-command PTY/child_process surface and a self-replacing remote-upgrade mechanism gives the publisher (or anyone who compromises the publisher's infrastructure) a persistent remote shell and arbitrary code execution on every host that installs or runs this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
